analytical_vs_cycle_on_mixed.hypothesis: ANALYTICAL ranks gemv0 ({'id': 'gemv0', 'kind': 'GEMV', 'resource_class': 'DSP'}) as bottleneck; CYCLE_MODEL ranks gather0 ({'id': 'gather0', 'kind': 'GATHER', 'resource_class': 'LUT'}). analytical scores static occupancy (DSP/LUT/BRAM/URAM/HBM demand); the cycle model scores initiation interval and critical-path issue. A DSP-cheap irregular node can be a cycle-expensive bottleneck. A cheap-level ranking that an expensive level would reverse must not promote.
analytical_vs_cycle_on_mixed.promotion_rule: Agreement does not license promotion. Disagreement is first-class evidence and blocks treating the cheaper level as decisive.

analytical_vs_cycle_on_single_gemv.hypothesis: ANALYTICAL and CYCLE_MODEL agree on node ranking ['gemv0']. Agreement is weak evidence: both models can share the same blind spot.
analytical_vs_cycle_on_single_gemv.promotion_rule: Agreement does not license promotion. Disagreement is first-class evidence and blocks treating the cheaper level as decisive.

analytical_vs_functional_on_dead_node.hypothesis: ANALYTICAL ranks dead0 ({'id': 'dead0', 'kind': 'GEMV', 'resource_class': 'DSP'}) as bottleneck; FUNCTIONAL_SIM ranks live0 ({'id': 'live0', 'kind': 'MAC', 'resource_class': 'DSP'}). functional_sim costs only live dataflow (unreachable nodes contribute zero); the other level still costs static occupancy or issue. Dead nodes are a finding, not noise. A cheap-level ranking that an expensive level would reverse must not promote.
